newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel fixed sharply lower against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Shekel fixed sharply lower against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed sharply lower against the dollar on Wednesday as the U.S. currency soared to its highest levels in years on overseas markets, dealers said.

"The strong dollar is pushing the basket downwards. Israeli investors know that the Bank of Israel has no choice (but to intervene) and they are using the opportunity to sell dollars at the current level," said a dealer at Bank Hapolim.
The Bank of Israel intervened again today on a relatively large scale to support the basket and to keep it at seven percent below the diagonal rate, he said

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2970 shekels against 3.2840 shekels on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6218 shekels against 3.6210 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7747 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7871 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.0094 shekels against 2.0255 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2980 shekels.
